title: arrays of arrays of one-element arrays compare wrongly at -O3 when two comparisons of them are printed together
reproducer:
def main():
    var e = [[[1]]]
    var z = [[[0]]]
    print(e > z, e == z)
compiler: prints `False False` at -O3, the default; -O0, -O1 and -O2 print the right `True False`. Four levels and Bools fail the same way; two elements, two levels, one level, and `print(e > z)` alone are right
fixed: compares the elements one by one, as the pin does at -O0, -O1 and -O2, so it prints `True False`

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: prints `False False` at -O3 and `True False` at -O0 to -O2, as the pin does; Mojo 1.2.0 does too, and also gets two levels, [[1]] against [[0]], wrong at -O3
